findings.title: Copy-paste bug in working-hours end calculation
findings.body: In the newly added working-hours check inside `checkIfIsAvailable`, `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`. As `start === end`, the guard collapses to `slotStartTime < workingHour.startTime || slotStartTime > workingHour.endTime`, which never detects slots whose duration crosses the end of the working window. For any event longer than the gap between the slot start and the day's working-hour end (e.g. a 60-minute slot starting at 17:30 with working hours 9-17), the slot is treated as inside working hours and forwarded to the busy check, so it can be booked outside availability.

findings.title: Working-hours comparison uses UTC time/day against organizer-local working hours
findings.body: The working-hours guard compares `workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day())`, `slotStartTime.hour()` and `slotStartTime.minute()` against `workingHour.startTime/endTime`. `WorkingHours.startTime/endTime` are minutes since midnight and `days` is the organizer/day-local day-of-week (as produced by `getAggregateWorkingHours`/`getWorkingHours`), while `slotStartTime` was produced by `time.utc()`, so `.day()/.hour()/.minute()` are in UTC. The comparison only works when organizer TZ is UTC; for any other organizer timezone the day-of-week and time-of-day values do not line up and slots can be classified as in/out of hours purely based on the UTC clock. The slot must be converted to the organizer's timezone (or, in `checkIfIsAvailable`, to `organizerTimeZone`) before these comparisons.

findings.title: Date-override day comparison formats in the server's local timezone
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` formats the shifted instant using the dayjs instance's default (server-local) timezone, not `organizerTimeZone`. The right-hand side `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` is also in the server's local zone, so the two sides happen to match each other but not necessarily the organizer. When an organizer whose timezone is east of UTC enters an early-morning override (e.g. 06:30 IST = 01:00 UTC), `add(-330)` crosses midnight and the formatted day is the previous UTC day, so slots on the correct organizer day are rejected as outside the override. Use `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).format("YYYY MM DD")` and `slotStartTime.tz(organizerTimeZone).format("YYYY MM DD")` to compare days in the organizer's timezone.

findings.title: `===` on dayjs instances never matches, breaking zero-length override handling
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` is reference equality of two distinct dayjs objects, which is always false. The branch that returns `true` (treating the slot as outside the override because the override has no duration) is therefore unreachable. Use `.isSame()` or compare `.valueOf()` if the intent is a value comparison. As written, a zero-length override (or "all-day" override with equal start and end) cannot be matched and falls into the same path as ordinary ranges.

findings.title: Multi-override semantics: first non-covering override incorrectly blocks the slot
findings.body: The `dateOverrides.find(...)` loop returns the first override whose day matches and for which the slot is outside that override's range; the outer `if` then returns `false` (slot unavailable) regardless of whether another override for the same day does cover the slot. With several date overrides on the same day (e.g. 09-11 and 14-16), a slot at 09:30 is inside the first override but not the second, the find returns the second, and the slot is rejected. The semantic should be ANY (available if any override covers), not ALL. The simplest fix is to break out as soon as a covering override is found, and only return `false` if every override for that day fails to cover.

findings.title: `dayjs.tz(date.start, override.timeZone)` used without guarding undefined
findings.body: `override.timeZone` was just made optional on `TimeRange`, but `slots.ts` calls `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` unconditionally. `dayjs.tz(..., undefined)` does not throw on every code path but yields the host-local offset, which silently corrupts the offset math (`organizerUtcOffset`) and therefore every converted override time, producing wrong `startTime`/`endTime` minutes and wrong slots. Either require `timeZone` on the input, default it to `organizerTimeZone`/`timeZone`, or assert/throw when it is missing so the failure is not silent.

findings.title: Convoluted offset arithmetic obscures intent and is easy to break under DST
findings.body: `const utcOffset = dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1;` followed by `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` is a non-standard way to express "view `date.start` in `organizerTimeZone`". It also relies on the offset at the exact instant `date.start`, so for multi-day date overrides that span a DST transition the start and end can be shifted by different amounts and the resulting window can be subtly incorrect. Replacing this with `dayjs(date.start).tz(organizerTimeZone)` (and equivalent on the slot) eliminates the manual offset handling.

findings.title: No test for the round-robin fixed-host date-override fix
findings.body: The PR description and linked issues (#8207, #8329) state the change makes fixed hosts' date overrides count toward round-robin availability, but the new test only covers a single user with a date override at two different invitee timezones. There is no scenario that exercises a round-robin event with a fixed host plus a round-robin host where the fixed host has a date override restricting availability on a day; that is precisely the behaviour being fixed and currently has no regression test.

findings.title: New `workingHours` branch in `checkIfIsAvailable` has no coverage
findings.body: The PR adds a `workingHours`-based availability check inside `checkIfIsAvailable` (slots.ts lines 138-151). None of the tests in `getSchedule.test.ts` cover that branch (no test sets up a schedule with a normal-hours entry and then exercises a slot that crosses or falls outside those hours, and none cover the UTC-vs-organizer-tz interaction). Given the day/time-of-day handling bugs above, this is the branch most likely to regress silently and is exactly where a regression test belongs.
